note: Hand-entered and checked by web search on the asOf date (sources in docs/DATA_SOURCES.md). Members are ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes; organisations that belong to a bloc (the EU and African Union in the G20, the EU at the G7) are in `alsoIncludes`.

blocs.name: NATO
blocs.about: Military alliance whose members commit to collective defence (Article 5). Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.

blocs.name: EU
blocs.about: Political and economic union of 27 states with a single market. The UK left on 31 January 2020.

blocs.name: G7
blocs.about: Annual summit of seven large advanced economies.
alsoIncludes: European Union (attends, not counted as a member)

blocs.name: G20
blocs.about: Forum of 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union. The US, hosting in 2026, has not invited South Africa, which remains a member.

blocs.name: BRICS
blocs.about: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, enlarged in 2024 (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE) and 2025 (Indonesia). Saudi Arabia was invited in 2023 but has not confirmed membership, so it is not shown.

blocs.name: Commonwealth
blocs.about: Voluntary association of 56 states, most of them once part of the British Empire. Gabon and Togo joined in 2022.

blocs.name: Five Eyes
blocs.about: Intelligence-sharing alliance of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK and the US.

blocs.name: UN P5
blocs.about: The five permanent members of the UN Security Council, each with a veto.
